title: Re-measure the Linux epoll race under the current Bun pin (LCLI-648 moved 1.3.14 to 1.4.2 without re-measuring it)
description:
Filed on opum-agent's instruction of 2026-09-30 alongside the LCLI-659 GO, in its own words: "The workflow comment says LCLI-648 moved 1.3.14 to 1.4.2 without re-measuring the race. File that re-measurement as its own task, but do not change the pin. DEC-80 settled 'no Bun pin' on the win32 side, and a pin change is the operator's call through opum-doc, not mine."

WHAT THE WORKFLOW ITSELF SAYS, verbatim from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s ubuntu Test step: "Bun can race Linux epoll registration when isolated files concurrently construct streams over the process stdio fds. Both observations behind this guard were taken on the 1.3.14 floor; LCLI-648 moved the pin to 1.4.2 without re-measuring the race, so the retry stays until someone does." The guard has since grown a third signal (LCLI-659) for the race's third presentation -- per-test hangs inside a completed run -- which is a widening of the RETRY, not a measurement of the RATE.

WHY IT IS OWED NOW. On 2026-09-30 the race fired on five consecutive attempts of a single required context (opum-ai/lore-cli#446, head `d9a144f7`), which is what a retry cannot absorb: attempts 1, 2, 4 and 5 hit the six-minute wrapper twice each, and attempt 3 completed at the green runtime with three tests hung. Under the retry the job fails whenever the race is COMMON, as distinct from occasional, and this is the observation that says the retry's design assumption may no longer hold on the current pin.

WHAT TO MEASURE, and the method matters more than the answer: the RATE of the race under the pinned runtime against 1.3.14's, on the same suite and the same flags -- e.g. N runs of `bun test --isolate --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=10000` on the two pins, counting runs in which any test died at its per-test budget or the wrapper killed the suite. Bun's pin is not the only variable that could have moved since the 1.3.14 observations (runner image, the suite's own growth, the platform package set), so a rate difference is evidence FOR the pin being a candidate and not proof on its own.

A PIN CHANGE IS NOT THIS TASK'S OUTPUT. DEC-80 settled "no Bun pin" for the win32-x64 acceptance and that settlement is not revisited here; this task produces the measurement, and if the rate is materially worse on 1.4.2 the finding goes to the operator as a packet through opum-doc with the pin change priced -- it is their call, not this repository's.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The rate of the epoll race under the pinned runtime is measured against 1.3.14's on the same suite and the same flags, and both numbers are recorded here with the method that produced them.

If the measured rate is materially worse on the current pin, the finding is routed as a priced packet through opum-agent to opum-doc, and the pin is not changed by this repository on its own authority.

implementationNotes: INBOUND FROM LCLI-659, which closed with one criterion partially met. LCLI-659 fixed the retry (opum-ai/lore-cli#447) so the race third presentation no longer fails the ubuntu required context, but its diagnostic clause — identifying, for at least one hanging test, the thing it was waiting on — was not satisfied and is carried here deliberately rather than dropped. It is not reproducible locally: the two tests that died at 10s on CI run in 146ms and 585ms on this workstation, and the three failing files run 90 tests in 9.46s under the CI exact flags. Instrumenting a hang therefore needs a runner, which is the same instrumentation this task needs to measure the race RATE under the current pin. Take the two together.

RATE DATA POINT, 2026-09-30, from opum-ai/lore-cli#454 (a tracker-record-only diff; nothing in it can reach a test): the run's ubuntu lint/typecheck/test leg (run 36789389206) had BOTH attempts hang on the known Linux epoll race — attempt 1 exited 124, attempt 2 stalled in test/cli.test.ts's init-dispatch group and was killed at the 6-minute wrapper (whole-process hang, not an assertion failure) — so the one-retry guard failed the job by design. Re-running the failed job gave the labelled RETRY-GREEN: attempt 1 fired the race (exit 124), attempt 2 passed, and the guard's own warning annotation says so. That is three hangs across four attempts in one evening on this repository — live evidence for this task's rate question under the current Bun pin (1.4.2, moved by LCLI-648 without re-measuring), and the rate does not look rare. Recorded by the lore-cli session that took the run; the same data point was sent to opum-agent on 2026-09-30 evening.

RATE DATA POINT, 2026-10-01 (00:20-04:15Z), from one lore-cli session landing four PRs:

- #458 (tracker-only diff): run 36807490794 red -- both of the job's attempts hung; its rerun then produced the labelled RETRY-GREEN.
- #459 (tracker-only): run 36809132879 took FIVE runs to land -- the initial run plus three reruns, and every attempt set hung BOTH attempts: eight consecutive hung test-suite executions, every log naming the race and ending "attempt 2 ALSO failed after the race retry". A fresh push (new run 36812675935) passed first try, which is what finally landed the PR.
- #460 (the LCLI-662 source change): ubuntu job green on its first run; its tracker-only closure run 36812998250 then hung both attempts and needed one rerun to go green.

So in about four hours: 12 hung test-suite executions across 8 runs, against 2 clean first-try passes and 2 RETRY-GREENs. Two readings of the #459 shape are consistent with this evidence and this note does not settle which -- a property of that particular run (state reruns reuse) or the runner population during that window. What it does show is the guard's design assumption, that the race is occasional, not holding for a stretch long enough to block a tracker-only PR through four attempts.

Data point for the re-measurement. CI run 37414330981, job "lint · typecheck · test (ubuntu-latest)" 112109490227, head 7de45422 (LCLI-680, PR opum-ai/lore-cli#493): attempt 1 exit 124, attempt 2 failed after retry. BOTH bounded attempts hung inside a SINGLE job, so the built-in single retry did not absorb the race this time; the job went red until a manual rerun, which passed at 4m55s. The job log carries the tooling line "The known Linux epoll runtime race fired on attempt 1 (exit 124); attempt 2 follows. No per-test durations are listed because this presentation kills the run rather than individual tests." No (fail) lines existed at all, which is the hang presentation rather than a product failure.

LCLI-660 MEASUREMENT (AC1): the Linux epoll race rate under the pinned Bun 1.4.2 vs the 1.3.14 floor, measured head-to-head on ubuntu-latest CI.

METHOD. A throwaway push-triggered workflow on branch exp/lcli660-epoll-rate (never merged) ran 20 trials per pin. All 40 jobs started within 12 seconds (2026-10-06 07:56:20-32Z) and ran CONCURRENTLY, so both arms share one window and one runner population -- no time confound. Each trial ran ci.yml's ubuntu Test step's EXACT suite, flags and stdio with the retry REMOVED: timeout --kill-after=10s 6m bun test --isolate --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=10000 2>&1 | tee /tmp/out.log ; status = PIPESTATUS[0]. A trial counts as a RACE event when status=124 (the 6m wrapper killed a hung suite), or the suite COMPLETED with every failure hung at its per-test budget (ci-flake-classify.sh), or the EEXIST epoll_ctl line appears.

RESULTS (run 37432801910, head bc6445ac):
- 1.4.2 (PINNED): race in 10 of 20 runs. 9 ended exit 124 (whole-suite hang killed by the 6m wrapper); 1 completed with per-test hangs. Victims sit across unrelated files at their budgets -- e.g. LCLI-612 quote-safety cases ~30001ms, workspace source/reference cases ~10010ms, workspace indexed lifecycle 10736ms, lore scaffold 10011ms, version drift 10001ms, canonical npm package family 10025ms -- matching LCLI-660's recorded victim list.
- 1.3.14 (FLOOR): race in 0 of 20 runs. Every run had exactly ONE failure -- the LCLI-648 test "the pinned runtime parses a contextual keyword starting a larger expression" (~18-29s), a genuine product failure of running the suite on 1.3.14, NOT the race. No EEXIST, no exit 124, no hang victims.

So the pinned 1.4.2 is materially MORE race-prone than the 1.3.14 floor in this window -- the opposite of the retry guard's premise ("both observations behind this guard were taken on the 1.3.14 floor; LCLI-648 moved the pin to 1.4.2 without re-measuring"). AC2's condition is met.

METHOD FINDING, load-bearing for the number. Two earlier passes on the SAME branch captured the suite with a FILE redirect (> /tmp/out.log 2>&1) instead of piping through tee, and got 0/20 races on 1.4.2. Changing ONLY the stdio topology to CI's pipe reproduced 10/20. The race depends on the process-stdio fds being a stream (the guard's own words); a file redirect removes the condition. Any future rate measurement MUST pipe through tee.

CAVEATS / WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH.
1. Single window. The race is bursty (LCLI-660's own history: 12 hung executions across 8 runs on 2026-10-01, on 1.4.2), consistent with 10/20 but a second window could differ.
2. The absolute 1.4.2 rate may be inflated by running 40 jobs at once (fleet contention). The PIN COMPARISON is unaffected -- both arms ran under identical contention and started together.
3. It CONTRADICTS the guard's premise that the race was seen on 1.3.14. Either the trigger changed between 1.3.14 and 1.4.2, or 1.3.14's isolate/topology avoids it, or the original 1.3.14 observations used a different config. Unresolved here; a cheap follow-up is to drop test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts from the 1.3.14 arm to rule out its single failing test as a confound.
4. The mechanism is NOT investigated -- this is a rate measurement, not a root cause.

PIN CHANGE IS NOT MADE HERE and is not this repo's call (AC2). The trade-off a packet must price is real in BOTH directions: 1.4.2 fixes a genuine 1.3.14 runtime panic (the LCLI-648 contextual-keyword case) but races in ~50% of runs here; 1.3.14 did not race in 20/20 here but re-introduces that panic. The experiment workflow is reproducible from this note; the branch exp/lcli660-epoll-rate is a deliberate throwaway and may be deleted.

LCLI-660 SECOND WINDOW (leader instruction 2026-10-06). Same workflow as window 1, 20 trials per pin, concurrent, CI-exact suite/flags/stdio with the retry removed, WITH one change: test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts excluded from BOTH arms so the arms run identical suites and the 1.3.14 arm's only window-1 failure (the LCLI-648 contextual-keyword test) cannot confound. Run 37437884748, head 03943708.

RESULT.
- Bun 1.4.2 (PINNED): race in 17 of 20 runs -- 13 as exit 124 (the 6m wrapper killed a hung suite) and 4 as the completed per-test-hang presentation.
- Bun 1.3.14 (FLOOR): race in 0 of 20 runs -- all 20 GREEN.

With the LCLI-648 test excluded, 1.3.14 is 20/20 clean, which CLOSES window 1's confound: 1.3.14 does not race, and its window-1 failures were entirely that one product test. Two windows now agree:

| window | 1.4.2 race | 1.3.14 race |
| 1 (full suite) | 10/20 (9 timeout + 1 hang) | 0/20 (each 1 fail = the LCLI-648 product test) |
| 2 (LCLI-648 excluded, identical suites) | 17/20 (13 timeout + 4 hang) | 0/20 (all green) |

ENVIRONMENT, both arms and both windows: runner image ubuntu-24.04 version 20260927.320.1, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, ImageOS ubuntu24. Window 1's kernel was not recorded -- its workflow did not print uname -r; its image version was read from the job header.

METHOD NOTE (kept because it cost a run and nearly a wrong number). Excluding the test with `rm` produced a one-fail "product" failure on BOTH arms: test/repository-location.test.ts reads every path `git ls-files` returns, and a working-tree-only delete leaves a TRACKED-but-missing path, so it threw ENOENT (measured in run 37437008715, 14/20 on 1.4.2 and 18/20 on 1.3.14 -- which read as an arm difference until the log was opened). `git rm` (index included) fixes it. Any file-exclusion control must keep `git ls-files` honest. The corrected run is the one reported above.
